## Unreleased

- **[data/breaking]** 233 previously served agreements removed: 167 filings outside the dataset's scope and 66 duplicates. agreements now holds 1,610 rows with status = 'invalid'.
  - Outside the dataset's scope (167): sponsor drop-downs to a controlled MLP or affiliate, guaranties, voting and support agreements, subscription, registration-rights and note-purchase agreements, financing documents, unexecuted forms and bidder proposals, amendments, proxy statements and an option plan, and 6 side agreements rather than acquisitions (PIPEs, a recapitalization, a block share sale, a JV contribution and a financing). Their sections, counsel, clauses and index rows are removed, and so is the XML of all but those 6, whose latest XML stays with status 'invalid'; the agreements row stays, with status = 'invalid', so the filing is not re-ingested. Duplicates (66 served; 70 agreements rows deleted in all, counting 4 duplicates from the EDGAR queue review): 65 originals superseded by their amended and restated version, which is now served under its own agreement_uuid, and 1 agreement filed twice (the earlier copy is kept). These agreements rows are deleted. In the previous release no agreements row had status 'invalid'; now 1,610 do (1,346 rejected in the EDGAR queue review, the 167 removed above, 31 rejected new filings, and 66 filings that were never served, rejected after their XML failed validation or was never built).
  - Tables: agreements, xml, sections, latest_sections_search, latest_sections_search_standard_ids, agreement_counsel, agreement_index_summary, clauses, tax_clause_assignments
  - Migration: Count or join served agreements through latest_sections_search or agreement_index_summary. Do not derive them from agreements: a plain COUNT(*) includes 1,610 invalid rows and other unserved filings, and status is NULL on most served agreements, so `status <> 'invalid'` drops them. 70 agreement_uuid values from the previous dump no longer exist; for the 65 amended and restated replacements, look the deal up by target and acquirer.
- **[data/breaking]** Section text and structure corrected across the corpus: of the 9,554 agreements served in both releases, 4,853 have changed words, 330 have a different number of sections and 2,598 have a changed outline; 663 keep identical section text, though their titles may differ.
  - Every served XML was rebuilt with the current builder (see the refs below), and at least 1,844 agreements (1,811 of them served, 1,141 continuing) also had hand-reviewed corrections to their heading tags, page labels or source text (23,317 text edits, 736 page-label edits). Main changes: (1) Page furniture is no longer served as section text: running titles, page numbers, document IDs, "Execution Version" and confidentiality legends ("confidential treatment requested ... omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission"), table-of-contents headers repeated on body pages and EDGAR SGML markup. Across all the changes in this entry, 330,313 words were removed from section text in continuing agreements, 4,728 agreements lost at least one word and 522 lost 50 or more. (2) Headings not detected before are now their own sections: final sections folded into the one before, whole articles, sections printed without a number, back-to-back headings of the same kind, and closing sections that sat on a page labeled as a signature page. 282 agreements gained sections and 48 lost some (signature pages, exhibits and schedules that had been served as the last sections, or as the first ones from a table of contents); net +604 sections. Section and article titles were cleaned (cross-references no longer read as titles, glued words split, heading periods and separator dashes dropped), which changes the outline of 2,598 agreements. (3) Spacing and punctuation now follow the filed page: no space before closing punctuation, split ordinals and possessives rejoined ("3 rd" -> "3rd"), glued words separated, page-text lines the HTML prints as one block joined, table rows of malformed HTML emitted once, and HTML paragraphs kept in page order. 553 continuing agreements changed only in spacing or punctuation; 136,683 words were added in all (rejoined tokens and recovered text, including the definitions in (5)). (4) A final text pass changed 257 agreements (165 continuing, 92 newly served) with 5,179 text fixes, counted against the text just before that pass; the continuing ones are included in the counts above. In 210 agreements it repaired inline text (5,118 fixes): page furniture left inside sections, words split at a line break ("Sub- sidiary"), leftover Word field codes, glued references ("Section3.3"), and lost spaces and hyphens. In 44 it repaired headings and section structure (58 fixes): headings cut at an abbreviation, body text served as a title, and stray numbers or cross-references tagged as sections. In 3 it restored to the body a title, preamble and recitals that were served only with the table of contents, so those agreements now open at the start of the text. (5) Two builder changes were then rolled out, rebuilding 8,754 agreements. A paragraph cut by a page break is now one paragraph, with the page number and page id that split it placed after it: 3,485 continuing agreements keep exactly the same words, in a different order, and in nearly all of them only those page markers moved. Stray numbers are no longer promoted to sections, titles cut at an abbreviation or running past the heading now end where the printed heading ends, definitions printed before Article 1 are served as their own article-level section (25 agreements), and table-of-contents lines left above the preamble are no longer served as text (23 agreements). Conventions: an article that prints no sections is served as one untitled section holding the article's text (94 agreements have no titled section at all, up from 42; 32,953 untitled sections, up from 24,913; 3,028 sections have no text, up from 2,178); a signature block printed on the same page as the last clause stays in the body; the testimonium may sit inside the last section.
  - Tables: xml, sections, latest_sections_search
  - Migration: 96.7% of section_uuid values survive: 922,968 of the 954,483 previous ids still exist. 11,912 ids in 777 continuing agreements changed (resectioned agreements) and 19,603 belong to removed agreements. Re-fetch section ids rather than joining on ids saved from the previous dump; to find changed agreements, compare sections rather than whole XMLs: no continuing XML is byte-identical, while 728,908 of the 922,968 surviving sections (79.0%) are.
  - Refs: #175, #177, #227, #228, #229, #230, #231, #232, #233, #234, #235, #236, #237, #238, #239, #241, #242, #244, #245, #246, #248, #249, #250, #256, #257, b5a626a2, 54955dea, 5fc61492, 17706a9b
- **[data/breaking]** Deal parties and listing status corrected: acquirer changed on 2,961 and target on 1,817 of the 9,554 continuing agreements; acquirer_type on 796, target_type on 558, acquirer_pe on 217, target_pe on 430.
  - Parties now follow written rules applied to the whole corpus: the acquirer and target are the parties the agreement prints (a parent counts only when the preamble names it as a party, not when it appears only as a guarantor or owner; no roll-ups to a parent found only in SEC filings), a transitory merger subsidiary gives way to the parent named as a party while a printed buying vehicle stays as printed, a sponsor buying through a vehicle is stored as the printed sponsor funds, a portfolio company buying in its own name is stored as that company, and names are as at signing. In a de-SPAC the SPAC is the acquirer and the operating company the target, even where a new holding company is printed; in a merger of equals or a combination under a new holding company, the printed new parent or surviving company is stored. A printed unlisted subsidiary of a listed parent is a public acquirer; OTC-quoted companies are public; non-traded REITs and BDCs and blank-check shells without a quote are private. Most changes were checked against the agreement text by an independent second read before they were written. Missing parties among the served corpus: none (all 11,973 have target and acquirer). Type coverage: target_type 11,973 and acquirer_type 11,973 of 11,973. target_pe now counts only named buyout-style sponsors that hold a majority or a stated control group, not venture-capital, hedge, distressed or credit funds or a minority block. All 2,004 served targets stored at 1 were reviewed for venture backing, and hedge and credit holders were then swept by manager name, so a few of those may remain: 547 were set to 0, and 203 with an unclear investor stayed at 1. The final metadata review then returned 2 of the 547 to 1 (2 more are no longer served) and set 45 other served targets from 1 to 0. Of the 543 still at 0 (476 private, 67 public), against the previous release 356 went from 1 to 0, 78 were empty, 9 were already 0 and 100 are newly served. The final metadata review read every served agreement (the 11,973, plus the 6 side agreements later removed) against the agreement text and, where the text did not settle a field, SEC filings or a party's own announcement. Against the values stored just before that review, it changed at least one metadata field (parties, types, sponsor flags, prices, consideration, deal type, dates, deal status or industries) on 3,291 agreements and counsel on 334, or 3,497 agreements in all. These changes are included in the counts in this entry and in the price and counsel entries.
  - Tables: agreements, latest_sections_search, agreement_index_summary, agreement_filter_option_summary
- **[data/breaking]** Deal price, consideration and dates corrected: price total changed on 3,369, filled on 509 and cleared on 699 continuing agreements; consideration type changed on 849; deal type changed on 293; deal status filled on 172 and changed on 166.
  - Prices now mean the headline price at signing, including assumed or repaid debt, without earnouts or CVRs, and as signed (not as later amended). The headline comes from the signed agreement, except on public-target deals, where the value the parties announced at signing takes precedence (see the separate entry on announced values). Elsewhere a stock leg the agreement does not value is cleared, and so is the total. Where no single total is printed but its pieces are, the total is arithmetic on printed figures only (a per-share price times a printed share count, or cash plus separately stated assumed debt); a partial purchase is priced at what is actually bought; an agreement buying several separately printed companies lists them all as the target and sums their prices; and a deal priced in a foreign currency has a USD price only where the agreement or a party's release prints one. Legs follow the signed figures too: a leg the agreement does not print is empty. Price total coverage among served agreements fell from 89.4% (8,752 of 9,787) to 86.1% (10,306 of 11,973) for two reasons. Among continuing agreements 699 totals were cleared, mostly where the agreement does not value a stock leg, and 509 were filled (89.5% -> 87.5%). The 2,419 newly served agreements have lower coverage (80.4%). Stock price legs: 1,149 cleared, 504 changed; cash legs: 1,574 changed, 601 cleared; asset legs: 364 cleared. Of the cleared legs, 140 stock, 206 cash and 157 asset legs were stored zeros. Consideration type: 421 mixed deals are now cash and 404 now stock (a deal with one real form of payment is no longer mixed, and cash paid in lieu of fractional shares does not count as a second form); served deals marked mixed 3,193 -> 2,968 while the corpus grew by 2,186. Deal type: a two-step deal (a tender or exchange offer followed by a back-end merger) is now tender_offer, so 272 continuing agreements moved from merger to tender_offer. Deal status: 156 empty and 124 pending deals are now complete, 34 pending and 15 empty now cancelled (a deal that went dark, delisted or passed its deadline without closing is cancelled); empty deal_status among served agreements 182 -> 3. Close date filled on 281, changed on 110 and cleared on 33 (it is the last closing of a staged deal, and empty where sources give only the month); announce date changed on 181 and filled on 11 (it is the announcement of the signed agreement, not of an earlier offer).
  - Tables: agreements, latest_sections_search, summary_data, agreement_ownership_deal_size_summary, agreement_ownership_mix_summary, agreement_buyer_type_matrix_summary, agreement_industry_pairing_summary, agreement_counsel_leaderboard_summary
  - Migration: Sums and medians of transaction_price_total change, and fewer deals have a total; the summary tables were rebuilt from the corrected values.
  - Refs: #179, 65a87fcb
- **[data/breaking]** transaction_price_total on 1,528 deals, 1,510 of them with a public target, was set to the value the parties announced at signing, including the debt-inclusive headline where one was stated; 1,522 still hold it after the final metadata review; the cash and stock legs moved with it only on 240 single-form deals.
  - On public-target deals, the value stated in the announcement press release or filing at signing now takes precedence over per-share arithmetic or a closing-date value when they differ by more than 5%: 1,409 totals changed and 119 were filled, measured against the value stored before this pass. The final metadata review then changed 4 of these totals and cleared 2. Against the previous release, 1,372 changed, 91 were filled, 10 match and 2 were cleared among the 1,475 continuing agreements; the other 53 are newly served. Where the release states a value including assumed or repaid debt, or the deal's enterprise value, the total holds that figure. The final metadata review also took a value from a party's own release page or investor deck where EDGAR holds none; a combined-company or pro forma value never counts. Mixed cash-and-stock deals whose agreement does not value the stock get the announced total, and the stock leg stays empty. On 240 single-form deals the cash or stock leg moved with the total: 17 were checked against share counts, and on the other 223 the value is at most 25% above the prior leg and can include some debt. 15 further legs were corrected from the filings. All other legs are untouched by this entry. After the final metadata review, 228 of the legs set from the announced value still hold it. These totals come from the release, not the agreement, and metadata_sources cites it. A deal with no announced value in the filer's own announcement filings keeps its existing total, so across public targets the field holds a debt-inclusive value on some deals and an equity value on others. Other private-target deals are unchanged by this entry. The 1,475 continuing agreements are included in the price counts in the entry above.
  - Tables: agreements, latest_sections_search, summary_data, agreement_ownership_deal_size_summary, agreement_ownership_mix_summary, agreement_buyer_type_matrix_summary, agreement_industry_pairing_summary, agreement_counsel_leaderboard_summary
  - Migration: transaction_price_total need not equal the sum of transaction_price_cash, transaction_price_stock and transaction_price_assets: it exceeds the legs by more than 1% on 1,849 served agreements and falls below them by more than 1% on 57. Do not test total = cash + stock + assets, and do not treat the gap as an exact debt figure. The legs are the closest measure of what holders receive, with three limits: on the 228 deals above the leg holds the announced value; a leg is empty where the agreement does not value it (the stock leg on 547 served mixed deals that have a total); and 287 served deals with a total have no legs. No field gives a like-for-like equity value across all deals. Sums and medians of deal value change; the summary tables were rebuilt from the new values.
- **[data/breaking]** Counsel rebuilt from each agreement's notices section: counsel changed on 1,634 continuing agreements and filled on 239; links 18,619 -> 24,424, firms with a link 1,398 -> 1,759 (the counsel table holds 1,854 rows; 95 have no link).
  - Counsel is the law firm the agreement's notices clause copies for each side ("with a copy, which shall not constitute notice, to"). Strings that joined two firms were split, variants, renames and offices of one firm were folded into one counsel row (never across a merger of two firms), and counsel that appears only elsewhere was dropped. 19 continuing agreements lost all counsel (the notices name none). Served agreements with any counsel: 9,208 of 9,787 (94.1%) -> 11,479 of 11,973 (95.9%).
  - Tables: agreement_counsel, counsel, agreements, latest_sections_search, agreement_filter_option_summary, agreement_counsel_leaderboard_summary

- **[mcp/breaking]** MCP tools are tuned for progressive tool discovery in Claude and Codex: self-contained descriptions, standard annotations, a task-to-tool map in the instructions, a compact get_server_capabilities default, and result data in the text content.
  - Clients that load tool definitions on demand (tool search) show the model only tool names and the server instructions up front, then one tool at a time. Each tools/list description now ends with that tool's "Use when" guidance and an "Avoid" list, which before lived only in annotations and get_server_capabilities. annotations now carries only the standard MCP hints (title, readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint); the custom selectionHint, negativeGuidance, pagination and requiredScopes keys are gone, with scopes and pagination moved to _meta as pandects/requiredScopes and pandects/pagination. Each tool gains a title, the non-standard top-level examples field is removed from tools/list, and filter arguments that had no description now have one. The initialize instructions map every tool to the job it does. get_server_capabilities with no arguments now returns a compact index (server, auth_help, changelog, a new one-line-per-tool tool_index, workflows, and sections_available); field_inventory, concept_notes and tool_limitations must be requested by name, and a new tool_names argument narrows the per-tool sections. Tool results now carry the data as JSON in a second text block after the one-line summary, so clients that show the model only content (not structuredContent) get the data too; results over 250,000 characters get a short note there instead. The pandects://capabilities resource returns the same compact index. On search_sections, search_agreements, list_agreements and search_tax_clauses, argument descriptions are shorter so each input schema fits the 5,000 bytes Codex allows before it strips all of them, and transaction_price_stock, transaction_price_cash and transaction_price_assets no longer repeat the bucket enum (their labels are the ones on transaction_price_total; other values are still rejected). search_agreements no longer advertises cursor or include_xml, which it accepted but ignored. get_server_capabilities reports unknown section names under unrecognized_sections.
  - Migration: Clients that read annotations.requiredScopes or annotations.pagination should read _meta["pandects/requiredScopes"] and _meta["pandects/pagination"]. Pass sections=["field_inventory", "concept_notes", "tool_limitations"] to get_server_capabilities to get the sections the old default included.
- **[schema/notable]** latest_sections_search.target and .acquirer widened from varchar(512) to varchar(1024); their two indexes now cover the first 600 characters.
  - Some acquirer lists (sponsor consortia and their printed funds) are longer than 512 characters; the longest served acquirer is now 882 characters and 7 served agreements exceed 512 in one of the two columns (6 acquirers, 1 target). idx_lss_target_section and idx_lss_acquirer_section are now (target(600), section_uuid) and (acquirer(600), section_uuid) instead of full-column indexes. agreements.target and .acquirer (varchar(2048)) are unchanged.
  - Tables: latest_sections_search
  - Migration: A plain restore of the dump needs no action, because the dump creates the table with the new definition. If you load the data into a table you created yourself, change the columns and the indexes together first; a full index on varchar(1024) is too long for InnoDB in utf8mb4: `ALTER TABLE latest_sections_search DROP INDEX idx_lss_target_section, DROP INDEX idx_lss_acquirer_section, MODIFY target varchar(1024) NULL, MODIFY acquirer varchar(1024) NULL, ADD INDEX idx_lss_target_section (target(600), section_uuid), ADD INDEX idx_lss_acquirer_section (acquirer(600), section_uuid);` With the old varchar(512) columns, the rows of those 7 agreements fail to load, or are cut at 512 characters outside strict SQL mode. Equality and prefix lookups return the same rows as before, but sorting on these columns can no longer be read from the index.

- **[data/notable]** The xml table in the dump now holds only each agreement's latest XML version (latest = 1); previous dumps also included some superseded versions.
  - The dump carries one xml row per agreement: its latest version, whether verified or not. Superseded versions stay out of the dump. Sections, latest_sections_search and the API are all built from the latest version, so they are unaffected. reader_index rows and clauses.xml_version values that name a superseded version no longer have a matching xml row.
  - Tables: xml
  - Migration: Queries that joined on older xml versions should use the latest one (xml.latest = 1, joined on agreement_uuid). Filter on status = 'verified' for the current public text.
- **[api/notable]** Error responses now carry a machine code in `error` instead of the HTTP reason phrase.
  - Every /v1 error body is {"error": <code>, "message": <text>}. Generic errors used to put the HTTP reason phrase in `error` ("Bad Request", "Not Found", "Unprocessable Entity", ...); they now use stable snake_case codes: bad_request (400), unauthorized (401), forbidden (403), not_found (404), method_not_allowed (405), conflict (409), validation_error (422), rate_limited (429), internal_error (500), service_unavailable (503). Other statuses use the snake_case reason phrase. Codes that were already specific (validation_error, rate_limited, captcha_required, legal_required, ...) are unchanged. A 422 from query-parameter parsing now names the field in `message` ("page_size: Not a valid integer.") instead of a generic sentence. Status codes and the /mcp JSON-RPC errors are unchanged.
  - Migration: Clients that compared `error` to a reason phrase should compare it to the new code, or branch on the HTTP status.
- **[mcp/notable]** search_sections phrase queries for common language now return results instead of an error.
  - A phrase common enough to match a large share of the corpus -- "material adverse effect", "reasonable best efforts", "governing law" -- previously exceeded the database time bound and came back as a validation error telling the caller to add filters, which could not help. Phrase mode now picks between two query plans per search, so these queries return normally. Two consumer-visible consequences: the error text for a phrase that still cannot be served now asks for a longer or more distinctive phrase rather than filters, and for the most common phrases total_count is reported as a lower bound with method `filtered_lower_bound` and planning_reliability `low`, because an exact count of those matches is not affordable. Read total_count together with has_next on those searches; count_mode=exact degrades the same way rather than failing. Result rows and their order are unchanged.
- **[api/notable]** /v1/search/agreements now applies text_query, and rejects metadata with a 422.
  - text_query and text_match_mode (phrase, all_terms, any_terms) were accepted on /v1/search/agreements but silently ignored, so a text search returned every agreement matching the other filters. An agreement now matches when at least one of its latest sections matches the text (and, together with standard_id or section_uuid, when one section matches all of them). match_count counts those sections, matched_sections previews the first three in document order with a snippet centered on the match, and each preview carries a new matched_terms list of the matched spans. When an exact count is not affordable, total_count is a lower bound (total_count_is_approximate true, count_metadata.method filtered_lower_bound); read it with has_next. A text query too expensive to serve returns a 422 on text_query. The metadata parameter, previously accepted and ignored, now returns a 422: every result already carries the full agreement metadata. Responses also gain count_metadata, and dump_version on searches without section criteria.
- **[api/notable]** Section search and GET /v1/sections/{section_uuid} exclude gated, unverified agreements.
  - /v1/sections and GET /v1/sections/{section_uuid} now apply the same public-eligibility rule as the agreement endpoints, which already hid agreements that are gated and not yet verified. A section of such an agreement no longer appears in search results and returns 404 when fetched directly. The MCP get_section, get_sections_batch, and get_agreement tools apply the same rule.
- **[api/notable]** An unknown price bucket is a 422 instead of being ignored.
  - transaction_price_total, transaction_price_stock, transaction_price_cash, and transaction_price_assets accept only the canonical bucket labels (0 - 100M, 100M - 250M, 250M - 500M, 500M - 750M, 750M - 1B, 1B - 2B, 2B - 5B, 5B - 10B, 10B - 20B, 20B+). Any other value (for example "1B - 5B") used to be dropped silently, so the request returned results unfiltered by price. /v1/sections, /v1/search/agreements, /v1/agreements, and /v1/tax-clauses now answer 422 validation_error, and the message names the field, the rejected value, and the valid labels. The MCP search_sections, search_agreements, list_agreements, and search_tax_clauses tools return the same detail as a -32602 invalid-arguments error. The OpenAPI spec lists the labels as an enum.
  - Migration: Send one of the listed labels; list_filter_options (MCP) returns them under transaction_price_totals.
- **[schema/minor]** New table reader_index: the outline, defined terms and cross-references of each verified XML version of an agreement.
  - One row per indexed XML version (composite key agreement_uuid, xml_version), so older versions are included. Join on xml with latest = 1 to get the row for the served text. payload_gz holds gzip-compressed JSON with the outline, defined terms with their declarations and uses, and cross-references with their status and target, all as stand-off anchors (container uuid, text ordinal and UTF-16 span) into that XML. Count columns and body_section_level_rate summarize each row without parsing the payload.
- **[api/minor]** New GET /v1/agreements/{agreement_uuid}/reader-index returns the reader index for the XML version the agreement endpoint serves.
  - The response holds no agreement text, only anchors into the XML that /v1/agreements/{agreement_uuid} returns. It is gzip-encoded when the client accepts it and carries a weak ETag for If-None-Match. For anonymous callers it follows the same focus_section_uuid and neighbor_sections window as the XML: term uses and cross-references in redacted text are left out, and declarations there are reduced to {"redacted": true, "label": "Section 1.1"}. Returns 404 when no index has been built for the current XML version.
- **[api/minor]** Keyword searches are capped server-wide and answer 503 with Retry-After when busy; an auth database outage answers 503, not the access-lockdown 403.
  - Text searches (text_query on /v1/sections and /v1/search/agreements, and the MCP search_sections tool) share a server-wide limit on concurrent full-text queries. A search that cannot start within a few seconds gets 503 with a Retry-After header and the message "Keyword search is busy right now. Please try again in a few seconds."; the MCP tool returns a -32004 error marked retryable with the same message. /v1 JSON error responses now keep the headers the error sets (Retry-After, Allow). When the auth database fails while checking a request's session or API key, the temporary access lockdown answers 503 "Auth backend is unavailable right now." instead of 403; requests without credentials still get 403.
- **[mcp/minor]** MCP OAuth hardening: client_name is validated, consent requires a registered redirect URI, and Deny goes through /authorize.
  - POST /v1/auth/oauth/register now rejects a client_name that is not a string, is longer than 255 characters, or contains control, formatting, invisible, or line-separator characters, or long runs of combining marks, with 400 invalid_client_metadata. A name over 255 characters, or one with an unpaired surrogate, previously failed with a server error. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed, and a name that is only whitespace is stored as no name. POST /v1/auth/oauth/consent now requires redirect_uri and returns 400 unless it is registered for the client. The new GET /v1/auth/oauth/consent/client returns a client's registered name and redirect URIs for the consent screen, which no longer reads the client's name from its own address. The consent screen names a known application only when every registered redirect URI is on that application's host, lists any other hosts that can receive access, and warns about unrecognized applications and names that claim a known client. GET /v1/auth/oauth/authorize accepts deny=1: once the client and redirect URI match the registration, it redirects to that redirect URI with error=access_denied and the state. A loopback redirect URI that differs from the registered one only by port must otherwise be well formed (no backslash, userinfo, or fragment), as at registration. The consent screen's Deny button uses it instead of sending the browser to the redirect URI in the page address.
- **[mcp/minor]** MCP OAuth /authorize reports an unsupported scope to the client as an invalid_scope redirect.
  - GET /v1/auth/oauth/authorize used to answer a request for a scope the server does not support with a JSON 400 shown in the browser, before it had checked the client or redirect URI. It now validates the client and redirect URI first and, as RFC 6749 section 4.1.2.1 requires, redirects back to the client with error=invalid_scope, the original state, and an error_description that names the scope when it is a well-formed scope token of at most 64 characters. A request with an unknown client or unregistered redirect URI still gets an error page and is never redirected. The consent endpoint keeps its 400 for unsupported scopes.
- **[mcp/minor]** MCP OAuth token and client-registration errors now use the codes the OAuth RFCs define.
  - POST /v1/auth/oauth/token errors return {"error", "error_description", "message"} with the RFC 6749 codes invalid_request, invalid_client, invalid_grant, unauthorized_client and unsupported_grant_type. POST /v1/auth/oauth/register errors use the RFC 7591 codes invalid_redirect_uri and invalid_client_metadata. Errors from both endpoints carry Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache. Both used to return the generic bad_request code. A code or refresh token whose Pandects account is not verified is now 400 invalid_grant instead of 403. `message` still carries the same text. The /.well-known OAuth discovery endpoints now return the standard error envelope codes (not_found, service_unavailable) instead of HTTP reason phrases.
  - Migration: MCP clients that follow the OAuth RFCs need no change. Code that matched `error == "bad_request"` on these two endpoints should match the RFC code or the status.
- **[docs/minor]** The published OpenAPI spec now matches what the API returns.
  - The spec at /openapi.yaml is regenerated from the API on every change (CI fails when it is stale), so it now documents the endpoints and parameters added since the last manual export, including /v1/taxonomy/counts and /v1/taxonomy/tax-clauses/counts. The `Error` schema now describes the real error body, {"error": <code>, "message": <text>}, instead of flask-smorest's {code, status, message, errors}. Response fields that are always present are marked required, and target_pe / acquirer_pe are documented as the 0/1 integers (or null) the API returns. Responses themselves are unchanged.
- **[api/minor]** REST responses carry industry and taxonomy labels next to the raw codes.
  - Agreement rows on /v1/agreements, /v1/agreements/{uuid}, and /v1/search/agreements gain target_industry_label and acquirer_industry_label: the NAICS description of the code (a code with no catalog entry of its own rolls up to its 2-digit sector; null when it cannot be resolved). The /v1/sections result metadata block gains the same labels for the industry fields that were requested. Section results, /v1/sections/{uuid}, /v1/agreements/{uuid}/sections, and /v1/search/agreements matched_sections gain standard_id_labels, a {standard_id: label} map for the clause-taxonomy ids in standard_id. Tax-clause results on /v1/tax-clauses gain tax_standard_id_labels for tax_standard_ids, and the agreement and section tax-clause lists gain standard_id_labels for standard_ids. /v1/filter-options gains industry_labels ({code: label}) whenever target_industries or acquirer_industries is returned. Existing fields are unchanged; callers no longer need /v1/naics or /v1/taxonomy just to print a label.
- **[api/minor]** New /v1/taxonomy/counts and /v1/taxonomy/tax-clauses/counts endpoints.
  - GET /v1/taxonomy/counts returns {"counts": {standard_id: n}}: how many sections /v1/sections?standard_id=<id> matches for each clause-taxonomy node, a parent counting the distinct sections tagged with it or any descendant. GET /v1/taxonomy/tax-clauses/counts returns the same shape for the tax-clause taxonomy, counting the clauses /v1/tax-clauses?tax_standard_id=<id> matches with default options (rep-and-warranty clauses excluded). Nodes with no matches are omitted.
- **[api/minor]** The clause_types field of /v1/filter-options is deprecated in favor of /v1/taxonomy.
  - clause_types has always returned the same tree as GET /v1/taxonomy; both now come from one builder and one cache. clause_types keeps working for existing callers, but new code should read /v1/taxonomy, which is cacheable on its own. The Pandects web client no longer requests clause_types.
- **[api/minor]** /v1/agreements-summary now reports processed_agreements alongside agreements.
  - The new processed_agreements field counts the agreements that have been processed and can be browsed and searched (the rows behind /v1/agreements-index). The existing agreements field is unchanged and still counts every agreement ingested, including those pending processing or verification.
- **[api/minor]** An out-of-range page_size now returns the largest allowed page instead of 25 rows.
  - On /v1/sections, /v1/tax-clauses, /v1/agreements, /v1/search/agreements, and the MCP search_sections, search_tax_clauses, search_agreements, list_agreements, and list_agreement_sections tools, a page_size above the caller's ceiling (100 for signed-in and API-key callers, 10 for anonymous callers) is now clamped to that ceiling rather than reset to the default of 25. A page_size below 1 still falls back to the default. Requests within range are unchanged.
- **[api/minor]** /v1/agreements accepts year_min, year_max, filed_after, and filed_before.
  - The year and filing-date range filters already accepted by /v1/sections and /v1/search/agreements now work on /v1/agreements too, with the same semantics (filed_after inclusive, filed_before exclusive, YYYY-MM-DD). Every agreement endpoint and MCP tool now shares one metadata filter implementation, so the same arguments select the same agreements everywhere.
- **[api/minor]** Canonical id fields on single reads, sort_direction on the agreements index, dump_version on tax clauses.
  - GET /v1/agreements/{agreement_uuid} and the MCP get_agreement tool now return agreement_uuid. GET /v1/sections/{section_uuid} returns standard_id (the name used everywhere else); section_standard_id stays as a deprecated alias with the same value. /v1/agreements-index accepts sort_direction like every other paginated endpoint; sort_dir keeps working as a deprecated alias, and sort_direction wins when both are sent. /v1/tax-clauses returns dump_version and accepts include_dump=false to omit it, as /v1/sections does.
- **[api/minor]** Search snippets no longer contain page numbers and page ids.
  - A section that crosses a page break carries <page> and <pageUUID> markers in its XML, and their contents leaked into /v1/search/agreements matched_sections[].snippet as text ("... more than 20 69 66af9b9a-20dc-11f1-ac97-be44a5e954c8 Business Days ..."). Snippets are now built from the agreement text only, so a text_query phrase that spans a page break also matches and is reported in matched_terms. The XML returned by the section and agreement endpoints is unchanged.
- **[mcp/minor]** Snippets and monetary_values ignore page numbers and page ids.
  - get_section_snippet, get_section_snippets_batch, get_sections_batch, and search_sections / search_agreements with snippets now drop the <page> and <pageUUID> markers before excerpting, so snippets read as clean text and a focus term that spans a page break is found. monetary_values is extracted from the same cleaned text.
- **[mcp/minor]** MCP industry labels roll an unlisted NAICS code up to its sector, as REST does.
  - target_industry_label / acquirer_industry_label (list_agreements, get_agreement, get_agreements_batch, search_sections metadata) and the list_filter_options industry_labels map used to match the code exactly, so a code with no catalog entry of its own (for example "459", "513", "922") was null in MCP while REST labeled it with its 2-digit sector ("Retail Trade" for "459"). Both surfaces now share one resolver. A non-numeric value or a code whose sector is also missing stays null.

  - Text search composes with standard_id and every structured filter. It is served from a private section_text_search table that is part of the production restore snapshot but not the public dump. Queries are capped at 256 characters and 24 terms, and each text-search statement runs under a 20-second database bound; a query that exceeds it returns a validation error asking for a narrower query.
  - Refs: 2d4c315, 7200bdb

  - Covers filings from late July through 14 August 2026. agreements 13,980 -> 14,126; latest_sections_search 947,546 -> 954,483. The section text search index tracks latest_sections_search row for row.

- **[api/minor]** Added changelog distribution: dumps/changelog.json is published next to each dump, GET /v1/changelog serves it (filterable by since/dump_sha256), and /v1/dumps entries gain changelog_url
  - Refs: 1eb2010
- **[mcp/minor]** get_server_capabilities gains a changelog section (latest release, breaking flag, URLs) and the initialize instructions point agents at it
